card.name: Jhumair
card.era: Traditional; agrarian roots in the Chota Nagpur plateau
card.tagline: Sadan harvest dance of the Chota Nagpur plateau
card.profile: Jhumair (Jhumar) is a folk dance of the Sadan - the Indo-Aryan ethnic groups of Chotanagpur - performed across Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Assam and West Bengal, and also by Adivasi communities, mainly associated with the harvest season (Wikipedia). Performers stand in a row or circle, hold hands, sing couplets, sway, clap and perform timed jumps, accompanied by the mandar, dhol, nagara and bansuri. Regional and stylistic varieties include Nagpuri, Khortha, Kurmali and Panchpargania Jhumar, plus the gendered Mardani (men's) and Janani (women's) Jhumar (Wikipedia; Historified).
card.insight: Folk artist Mukund Nayak of Jharkhand is a celebrated exponent of Nagpuri Jhumar, having taught and recorded the form for decades to preserve its Sadan roots (Grokipedia, citing Ranchi University records).

observation.dancers: group of male dancers and musicians, all adult men
observation.formation_and_space: curved line and semi-circle facing inward or toward a central group of drummers, moving in place with occasional shifts
observation.posture: upright torso with upright posture, knees slightly bent and bouncing with the beat, weight shifting actively between feet
observation.footwork: rhythmic stepping and hopping on the spot, jumping with both feet on beats, stepping side-to-side and heel touches; exact foot placements occluded by loose trousers
observation.arms_and_hands: arms held out to the sides or linked, holding small cloths or scarves in hands, moving up and down with the jump and step rhythm
observation.hips_and_torso: minimal torso isolation, bouncing torso along with knee bends and jumps
observation.partnering: none, solo styling within a group formation
observation.levels_jumps_turns: frequent small hops and jumps, a coordinated sequence where all dancers drop to one knee/squat on the ground and rise back up
observation.costume_and_props: matching red t-shirts, white dhotis or trousers, sashes across shoulders, headbands, and small cloths held in hand; drummers wear varied casual shirts and dhotis
